newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Brokers say Morocco bourse tax will not hit trade.
newsitem.headline: Brokers say Morocco bourse tax will not hit trade.

text.p: Moroccan brokers said on Wednesday that taxes imposed on the stock exchange to fund the bourse's watchdog Conseil Deontologique des Valeurs Mobilieres (CDVM) would have no direct effect on brokers or on trade.

A broker at Upline Securities brokerage said: "There is no direct impact on traders' commissions. But (for) local brokerages, being shareholders of the bourse, it will diminish their turnovers, but I do not think it will affect small shareholders."
He said foreign investors were not affected by the taxes.
Another broker, at BMCI Securities, said the new measure would only have a moderate effect on brokerage turnovers.

"There is nothing bad in having the CDVM get more money for its operations but the bourse shareholders fear that this creates a precedent so that every time an institution needs money it will turn to the stock exchange," he added.
The brokers said the taxes would come out of the 0.35 percent which the bourse gets from the one percent brokerage commissions.
A CDVM spokesman told Reuters on Monday that the body started imposing the taxes from July 1. Under a decree, the taxes are set at 0.04 percent on share trading and 0.02 percent on bond transactions.
The CDVM was set up in 1994 and had been up to now funded by commissions on public issues and on mutual funds, plus state subsidies, he said.
Among other aspects of its work, it has delisted 18 companies for not publishing their annual results.
At present, 48 stocks are listed on the exchange.
